claims.text: Donald Barr announced in Feb 1974 he would resign at the end of the school year; Epstein began teaching at Dalton in Sept 1974; whether Barr had any role in hiring him is not clear; Dalton did not respond; the mentor claim is unsupported.
Business Insider reported that Barr hired Epstein to teach maths and science; Dalton yearbooks of 1975 and 1976 show him; he left after two years.

Hoffenberg (serving 18 years) claimed Douglas Leese, a British defence contractor who died in 2011, mentored Epstein after Bear Stearns and introduced him to Adnan Khashoggi and allegedly Robert Maxwell; Leese's son says his father was a mentor of sorts but not an arms dealer; Leese appears in the UK parliamentary record re the Al Yamamah deal; in a Florida lawsuit Leese said he was involved in 'highly confidential business enterprises'; Epstein twice denied knowing Leese in 2002; Ward: she 'can't prove all of Hoffenberg's claims'; Epstein secretly cooperated with prosecutors against Hoffenberg.

NYT (Dec 2025): Epstein's connection to Wexner's friend Robert Meister, an insurance executive who sat next to him on a flight to Palm Beach, launched the friendship; Wexner's adviser Harold Levin warned 'I smell a rat'; Epstein had Levin fired; NYT: 'the biggest mystery is what exactly the billionaire got out of his relationship with Epstein'.

Wexner to House Oversight (Feb 2026): Epstein was suggested to him in the 1980s as a potential adviser; at first refused payment, 'as a favor'; 'from the very start, Epstein was conniving to gain my trust'; emails show contact in 2008 though he says ties ended about 2007; DOJ documents list him as a potential co-conspirator, which his representatives dispute.

Black met Epstein in the mid-1990s; paid about $158m 2012-17 per Apollo's review, which said the advice was worth more than $1bn; paid $62m to the USVI in 2023; walked out of a House interview in June 2026 over questions about NDAs, skipped a 16 July deposition and sued the committee; says he fired Epstein in 2018.

JPMorgan filing (June 2023): Financial Trust/Southern Trust received $219.8m in USVI tax benefits 1999-2012 and $80.6m 2013-18; Cecile de Jongh, wife of Governor John de Jongh (2007-15), managed Epstein's local companies for eight years, allegedly helped arrange visas, received salary, bonuses and tuition, and in 2009 certified him a 'bona fide resident' while he was serving his sentence; USVI says JPMorgan put profits first.
